beats.lead: The man who saved the world
beats.note: Accounts of how he was treated differ, but several describe a reprimand for how the incident was written up.

beats.name: Lieutenant Colonel Stanislav Petrov
beats.role: Duty officer at the Soviet Oko early warning centre. Shortly after midnight, the system reported a US missile launch.

beats.context: Oko showed one, then four more. Petrov doubted a real attack would start with five, and the new system had not earned his trust.

beats.note: Oko had misread sunlight reflecting off high altitude clouds as missile launches. A geostationary satellite later helped correct the error.
The incident stayed secret until the late 1990s.

beats.text: Five dots on a screen, a faulty sensor, and a man who waited for confirmation.

beats.line: Sometimes the best decision is waiting for proof.
